chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammam, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

Abbad ibn Abdillah al-Basri asked him about a man who made a vow to God that he would walk to the House of God (the Kaaba) with his own body. He walked half the way, whether a little or a lot. He said: 'He looks at what he had intended to spend from that place (where he stopped) and gives it in charity.'

key_terms.الْمَشْيَ: Walking (specifically on foot as a form of devotion)
key_terms.بَيْتِ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامِ: The House of God (the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.فَيَتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ: And he gives it in charity (fulfillment method)
key_terms.نَذْرًا: A vow or pledge made to God to perform a specific act of worship or charity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for fulfilling a vow of walking to the Kaaba if one stops halfway?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for a vow of walking to the Kaaba, the obligation is fulfilled by donating the unspent portion of the allocated travel expenses as charity, rather than completing the physical journey. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the essence of a vow is the expenditure of wealth for God's sake, allowing flexibility when the specific mode (walking) becomes burdensome or interrupted. It underscores the importance of intention and financial dedication in fulfilling nadhr, a concept deeply rooted in the practices of the Ahl al-Bayt.
